text.name: Mobile app · English: Avenir · Arabic: Frutiger LT Arabic
White & neutrals 65% · Ink for text & structure 25% · Red for accents & action 10%
Grey on White — Not for body text
Red on Fog — Not for small text
Success Dark on Success Light — Banner / toast text
Failure on White — Error messages, field hints
Failure Dark on Failure Light — Banner / toast text
Spacing follows an 8px rhythm with a 4px half-step. The 2, 4, 6 and 12px steps are for tight component internals only. Every padding and gap comes from a Spacing variable, never a typed-in number.
No space. Elements that sit flush, edge-to-edge images and full-width dividers.
Hairline gaps. Stacked lines inside a compact label, such as a title over its caption.
Micro gaps. Icon to small text, pill and chip padding, field to helper text.
Tight component internals that need a little more air than 4px.
Tightest gap. Icon to label, page-indicator dots, chip internals, status bar top inset.
Between list rows, option cards and keypad keys; padding inside small components.
Closely related items. Headline to message, stacked buttons, form label to field, list item content.
Default mobile screen margin (left/right). Button and card inner padding, component padding.
Separating groups. Footer bottom padding above the home indicator, space before a group of actions.
Between distinct sections inside one screen.
Large section breaks; matches the 48px top-bar and minimum touch-target height.
Hero spacing above or below key content on spacious screens.
Very large separation. Documentation sheet padding, empty-state offsets.
Rare. Extra breathing room on tablet or large layouts.
Rare. Empty-state and illustration offsets on large screens.
Rare. Full-screen moments such as splash and celebration screens.
Canvas only. Gaps between frames and sheets in Figma, not used inside the app.
Bind padding and gaps to spacing/* variables. Typed-in values break the system and won’t update.
Layouts use multiples of 8. Use 2, 4, 6 and 12px only inside components. If a gap feels wrong, step up or down the scale instead of inventing a value.
Use smaller steps inside a group and larger steps between groups, so structure is visible without dividers.
24px screen margins, 32px bottom padding above the home indicator, 16px between stacked buttons.
Corner radius comes from Radius variables. Steps follow a 4px sub-grid so small elements can round softly while larger surfaces stay on the 8px rhythm.
Square corners. Full-bleed images, edge-to-edge sections, dividers, top app bars.
Hairline elements. Progress dots, thin bars and dividers with soft ends.
Small details. Tags, badges, progress bars, tiny thumbnails.
Compact controls. Checkboxes, small inputs, tooltips, small icon buttons.
Default for controls. Buttons, text fields, dropdowns, small cards.
Containers. Cards, list groups, banners, toasts, rate and fee summary panels.
Large surfaces. Bottom sheets (top corners), dialogs, logo tile, large feature cards.
Hero surfaces. Promotional cards and large onboarding panels.
Large surfaces. Phone screen frames, illustration canvases and onboarding cards.
Fully rounded. Pills, chips, avatars, page-indicator dots, circular icon buttons.
Bind corners to radius/* variables instead of typing values, so a change to the scale updates every screen.
Radius grows with element size: controls md, containers lg, sheets and dialogs xl.
An inner element’s radius should be the outer radius minus the padding between them, so curves stay parallel.
For anything meant to be fully round, use radius/full rather than half the height, so it stays round when it resizes.
Line thickness comes from Stroke variables. UI strokes stay thin (1–2px) and step with icon size; heavier widths are reserved for illustrations and loaders.
Hairlines. Dividers, card and section outlines, toast borders, inactive outlines.
Icons 18px and smaller: inline validation, chips, helper rows, small badges.
Default. Icons 20–28px, outlined (Secondary) buttons, input borders.
Large icons 32px and up: hero icons and empty states.
State emphasis. Focused or error fields, checkboxes, dashed placeholders, progress rings.
Illustrations: badge rings and the ticks inside them.
Illustrations: scan corners, fingerprint ridges, badge marks.
Illustrations: accent strokes such as the camera-off slash.
Illustrations: heavy marks such as the success tick and padlock shackle.
Loaders: the progress arc on “Checking your details”.
Illustrations: knock-out outline behind the camera-off slash.
Never type a stroke width. Pick a stroke/* variable so one change updates every screen.
Icons up to 18px use sm, 20–28px use md, 32px and up use lg. Thin lines keep small icons from looking bulky.
Use xl only to show state: focus, error, selection or progress. Resting borders stay xs or md.
2xl to 8xl belong to illustrations and loaders only. Never use them on buttons, fields or icons.
